programme: A BMAL1-anchored circadian output (BMAL1 with its clock target NFIL3) coupled to two proteostasis stress-response arms, the ATF6 unfolded-protein-response branch and the TFEB autophagy-lysosome branch, that together gate how a stressed cell (infected or ischemic) handles misfolded protein and damaged organelle load and how it signals to circulating immune cells.
role_in_a: In COVID-19, SARS-CoV-2 infection dampens BMAL1-driven circadian transcription in infected cells (PMID 41927871, PMID 42304657), while the virus separately triggers ER stress that engages ATF6-mediated UPR (PMID 42085452, PMID 41798766, PMID 38785529) and dysregulates TFEB-driven autophagy-lysosome flux, a disturbance proposed to carry acute disease into Long COVID (PMID 41394849, PMID 40465712).
role_in_b: In stroke, BMAL1 is protective against cerebral ischemia via circadian control of neutrophil trafficking that shapes collateral perfusion and outcome (PMID 41005429, PMID 41293815, PMID 41440117); ATF6 activation confers long-term post-stroke benefit and preserves endothelial barrier integrity (PMID 40259100, PMID 35933031); TFEB-dependent autophagy limits neuronal damage and ferroptosis after ischemia (PMID 41876744, PMID 41272418).
shared_axis: Both an acute viral infection and an acute ischemic insult impose sudden proteotoxic and hypoxic stress on blood and vascular cells, and both engage the same BMAL1-anchored clock/proteostasis response (BMAL1-NFIL3 circadian output plus ATF6 UPR and TFEB autophagy) to manage misfolded-protein and organelle clearance and to time immune-cell trafficking through the vasculature. The axis is protective in each case on its own terms, not shared as a named disease mechanism between COVID-19 and stroke.
reasoning: BMAL1, ATF6 and TFEB are each independently documented in COVID-19 and separately in stroke by multiple retrieved papers, and one paper for each of BMAL1 and ATF6 touches both a vascular/endothelial theme and a circadian-immune theme relevant to both settings, so the module is nameable and partly placed in the record. NFIL3 only reaches co-dysregulation studies (PMID 37062762, PMID 39697434, PMID 38384585) rather than a mechanistic BMAL1-target role in this material, and no retrieved source states the four-factor axis as a shared COVID-19/stroke mechanism, so the connection between diseases rests on reasoning about shared acute-stress biology rather than on a documented joint claim.
support: PMID 41927871 and PMID 42304657 place BMAL1 circadian disruption in COVID-19; PMID 41005429, PMID 41440117 and PMID 41293815 place BMAL1 as protective and immune-timing in stroke, with 41293815 spanning both via circadian neutrophil control of stroke outcome; PMID 42085452, PMID 41798766 and PMID 38785529 place ATF6/UPR activation in coronavirus infection; PMID 40259100 places ATF6 activation as neuroprotective post-stroke and PMID 35933031 ties ATF6 to endothelial barrier protection relevant to both vascular settings; PMID 41394849 and PMID 40465712 place TFEB-autophagy dysregulation in acute and long COVID; PMID 41876744 and PMID 41272418 place TFEB-driven autophagy as neuroprotective in stroke; PMID 37062762, PMID 39697434 and PMID 38384585 show NFIL3 dysregulation in COVID-19 and stroke without a mechanistic link to the other three factors.
how_to_falsify: In parallel SARS-CoV-2-infected blood/endothelial cultures and an oxygen-glucose-deprivation (ischemia) model of the same cell types, knock down or pharmacologically inhibit BMAL1 and measure ATF6 UPR induction (spliced/nuclear ATF6 target genes) and TFEB nuclear translocation/autophagic flux in both systems; if the circadian-proteostasis coupling proposed here is real, BMAL1 loss should blunt both ATF6 and TFEB responses and worsen endothelial permeability or cell death in both the viral and the ischemic model, whereas ATF6/TFEB responses that persist unchanged after BMAL1 loss in either system would falsify the shared-axis account.
caveats: Only 4 independent cohort pairs underlie the 12 patient-group comparisons, and every listed factor sits at the same 8/12 (67%) concordance rather than near-universal agreement, so this is a moderate, not a dominant, signal. Both diseases are compared only in blood, so the stroke side is a peripheral proxy for what is mechanistically a CNS-vascular event, and no CNS tissue evidence is available here. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed core immune regulators (STAT1, STAT3, STAT5A, JUNB, SMAD3, EPAS1, LEF1, E2F1, ETS2, LITAF, HLX, CIITA), so this account deliberately does not lean on generic inflammatory drivers, and its absence of those names is by design, not an oversight. The single-view exclusions (developmental factors like HOXA13, PAX2, TBX6) are unrelated to this programme and played no role in shaping it. NFIL3's placement in the axis is the weakest link and should be treated as a peripheral, not load-bearing, member.
